title: SEBI Mutual Fund Categorization Guidelines FAQ
text: SEBI Mutual Fund Categorization Guidelines and Riskometer FAQ.  SEBI guidelines specify the classification of mutual funds into 5 broad groups: Equity, Debt, Hybrid, Solution-Oriented, and Other schemes.  - Riskometer: The Riskometer must have six risk levels: Low, Low to Moderate, Moderate, Moderately High, High, and Very High.  It must be evaluated monthly based on portfolio characteristics.

title: AMFI Mutual Fund Category Explanations
text: AMFI Mutual Fund Category Explanations.  Association of Mutual Funds in India (AMFI) Knowledge Center: - Equity Schemes: Invest primarily in shares/stocks.  Capped categories include Large Cap (top 100 stocks), Mid Cap (101-250th stocks), and Small Cap (251st and below).  - Debt Schemes: Invest in fixed income securities (treasury bills, government bonds, commercial paper).  - ELSS: A category of equity funds offering tax saving under Sec 80C with a 3-year lock-in.

title: AMFI Total Expense Ratio (TER) Rules
text: AMFI Total Expense Ratio (TER) Rules.  The Total Expense Ratio (TER) represents the annual operating expenses of a mutual fund scheme, expressed as a percentage of the fund's daily net assets.  25% for the first ₹500 Crores of AUM, scaling down as AUM increases.  - Regular vs Direct: Direct plans have a lower expense ratio since they do not include advisor commission or distribution costs.  Last updated from sources: May 2026.

title: AMFI Exit Load Rules
text: AMFI Exit Load Rules.  An exit load is a fee charged to investors when they redeem or switch out of a mutual fund scheme within a specified timeframe.  - Purpose: To discourage short-term trading and protect long-term investors.  - Calculation: Calculated as a percentage of the Net Asset Value (NAV) at redemption.  For SBI equity funds, the standard exit load is 1% if redeemed within 1 year, and Nil thereafter.  Last updated from sources: May 2026.
